title: Add unit tests covering the ceiling / unlimited / 404 branches
description: Add focused unit tests in `backend/tests/` for the new budget endpoint. The test file must follow the project's pytest + asyncio conventions and must cover at least these three branches on a real (in-tmp-path) `AsyncSQLiteStore`: (1) an issue with an explicit `budget_usd` ceiling — assert the response includes `spent_usd`, `budget_usd`, `remaining_usd`, `used_ratio`, `soft_warn`, `over_budget`, `soft_warn_ratio`, `has_ceiling`, `budget_source`, and that the spent is the sum of completed-run costs only; (2) an issue with `budget_usd <= 0` — assert `has_ceiling` is False, `remaining_usd` and `used_ratio` are None, `over_budget` is False; (3) a missing issue id — assert the endpoint raises `HTTPException` with status 404. Tests must run under the default `pytest` invocation (i.e. NOT marked `@pytest.mark.slow`).
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover the ceiling, unlimited, and missing-issue branches
Tests use the real AsyncSQLiteStore pattern (in tmp_path), not heavy mocks
Tests are NOT marked @pytest.mark.slow and pass under the default pytest lane

pinned_qa_commands.description: Run the budget endpoint tests; expect all 3+ branches to pass

argv: from pathlib import Path; text = Path('tests/test_issue_budget_endpoint.py').read_text(); assert '@pytest.mark.slow' not in text

notes: Test file naming follows the existing convention (test_<feature>_endpoint.py).
